title: Normal form of the specified cocone derived comparison
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $X$ any scheme, and $E\subseteq H\subseteq\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ finite intermediate extensions. Use the coefficient ring objects of [def-sfb-derived-extend-subfield] and [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar]; $\Omega_X$ is the pullback of the condensed ring whose continuous sections have image in one finite subfield. Write $\varphi:E_X\to H_X$, $\psi:H_X\to\Omega_X$, $\kappa:E_X\to\Omega_X$ for the coefficient inclusions, with $\psi\varphi=\kappa$ as in [lem-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map-comp]. In the internal module categories put $A=\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}$, $B=\operatorname{Ext}_{\psi}$, $D=\operatorname{Ext}_{\psi\varphi}$ and $C=\operatorname{Ext}_{\kappa}$, using [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Let $u:BA\xrightarrow{\sim}D$ be the unit-compatible comparison of their scalar-extension adjunctions with the canonically identified common right adjoint, as in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation], and let $e:D\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ be the specified coefficient-map equality comparison of [def-sfb-extend-scalars-iso-of-eq].

Write $L$ for the total left derived functor of an exact additive functor, with its specified localization comparison [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and let $c:L(BA)\xrightarrow{\sim}(LB)(LA)$ be the exact-derived composition comparison [lem-sfb-exact-derived-composition]. The fixed canonical cocone comparison $\delta$ constructed in [def-sfb-derived-extend-comp-iso] has the normal form
$$\delta=L(e\circ u)\circ c^{-1}:(LB)(LA)\xrightarrow{\sim}LC.$$
Here $L(e\circ u)$ denotes the induced natural isomorphism of [lem-sfb-exact-derived-natural-iso]. Under these identifications $LA=T_{E,H}$, $LB=T_{H,\Omega}$ and $LC=T_{E,\Omega}$ are the specified functors, with their object and arrow assignments; no additional automorphism of a derived functor is inserted. The equation concerns the specified construction, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism having the same endpoints.

proof.text: The functors $A,B,C$ preserve finite colimits by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars](2). They preserve finite limits by [lem-sfb-subfield-flat] (for $A$) and [lem-sfb-qlbar-flat] (for $B,C$), so they are exact additive scalar-extension functors. By [lem-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map-comp] the composite coefficient map is $\kappa$; [def-sfb-extend-scalars-iso-of-eq] gives the specified $e:D\cong C$. Thus $D$ is exact as well: transport each finite limiting or colimiting cone through the natural isomorphism $e$, use preservation by $C$, and transport back. The composite $BA$ is exact because applying $A$ and then $B$ preserves each such cone.

Let $R=\operatorname{Res}_{\psi\varphi}$. Restriction along $\varphi$ after restriction along $\psi$ has action $\gamma_N(\psi\otimes1)(\varphi\otimes1)=\gamma_N((\psi\varphi)\otimes1)$ and leaves every underlying arrow unchanged, by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars](1). Pasting the two adjunction Hom bijections in (2) gives $BA\dashv R$, with unit $\eta_{BA,M}=\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}(\eta_{B,AM})\circ\eta_{A,M}$. Also $D\dashv R$. In the fixed construction, denote by $s:D\cong BA$ the comparison called `Mod.extendScalarsComp`; its definition is left-adjoint uniqueness for these two adjunctions, after this very restriction identification. Therefore its defining unit equation is $R(s_M)\circ\eta_{D,M}=\eta_{BA,M}$, as in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]. Applying $R(s_M^{-1})$ gives $R(s_M^{-1})\circ\eta_{BA,M}=\eta_{D,M}$. The uniqueness clause of that node, now with $L_1=BA,L_2=D$, gives $s^{-1}=u$. The other underived factor is exactly $e$, by [def-sfb-extend-scalars-iso-of-eq], not just an unspecified comparison along the equal maps. Hence the underived isomorphism passed to derivation in the fixed definition is $\theta=e\circ s^{-1}=e\circ u$.

proof.text:
Write $a_J:(LJ)Q\cong QC(J)$ for the specified exact localization comparisons, and let $c_0:L(BA)\cong(LB)(LA)$ be the comparison used by the fixed construction. Its definition transports the localization comparison for termwise composition along the exact-functor identifications $LJ\cong D(J)$ of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. The termwise composition comparison comes from the identity $C(B)C(A)=C(BA)$. Consequently, cancelling the intervening exact-functor identifications and their inverses in this definition gives, on every complex $K$,
$$a_{B,C(A)K}\circ LB(a_{A,K})\circ c_{0,QK}=a_{BA,K}.$$
This is exactly the characterizing equation of [lem-sfb-exact-derived-composition] for the comparisons $a_J$ fixed here. Its uniqueness clause gives $c_0=c$. In particular, the first factor in the definition of $\delta$ is $c^{-1}$, in the direction $(LB)(LA)\to L(BA)$.

proof.text:
For $\theta:BA\cong C$ from step 2, let $n_0:L(BA)\cong LC$ be the second factor in the fixed construction. Expand its definition: it is the termwise natural isomorphism $C(\theta)$ localized, with the exact-functor identifications $L(BA)\cong D(BA)$ and $LC\cong D(C)$ on either side. Thus cancellation of these identifications yields
$$a_{C,K}\circ n_{0,QK}=Q(C(\theta)_K)\circ a_{BA,K}$$
for every complex $K$, with degree-$j$ map $\theta_{K^j}$. This is the characterizing equation of [lem-sfb-exact-derived-natural-iso]; uniqueness gives $n_0=L(\theta)$. The universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2)-(3) makes these comparisons equal as natural transformations on the entire derived category: equality after the localization functor detects equality, rather than merely giving isomorphic values on objects.

proof.text:
Unfold the fixed definition of $\delta$ (TwoColimit.lean:142-146): it is $n_0\circ c_0^{-1}$, with $\theta$ the underived composite read in step 2. Substituting steps 2-4 gives
$$\delta=L(e\circ u)\circ c^{-1}.$$
By [def-sfb-derived-extend-subfield] and [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar], the symbols $LA,LB,LC$ denote exactly the specified extension functors $T_{E,H},T_{H,\Omega},T_{E,\Omega}$. The substitutions above are equalities of natural transformations between these fixed functors, with their object and arrow maps, so they do not replace any functor by another chosen equivalent one. Any postcomposition by an automorphism would have to satisfy the same localization equation to preserve the specified construction; by the uniqueness in step 4 it would equal the identity. This proves the asserted normalization of the chosen comparison.
